content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) but underperform in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.5), especially when sentiment is high and recent.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 73+), leading to overcorrection in subsequent days — reduce forecast by 1–2% after a spike.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias: model tends to overpredict after recent highs and underpredict after recent lows — adjust forecast toward historical mean of last 5–7 days.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts: when sentiment turns negative, model takes 2–3 days to adjust downward — apply a 1–2% downward correction on day 3+ after sentiment drop.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent overestimation in early days (1–5) when sentiment is positive — reduce first 5 forecast points by 0.5–1.5%.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to overreact — dampen forecast by 0.5–1.0% for 3–5 days.
